security_audit.summary: The skill intentionally executes irreversible trades through an external CLI and relies on API and wallet private keys stored in a hidden environment file. Most backtick findings are Markdown false positives, but credential solicitation, secret access, financial commands, network reconnaissance, and confirmation bypasses are confirmed. Publication should wait until credential collection and transaction approval controls are redesigned. Static review was capped at 400/430 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 30 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: The setup flow asks users to send an API key and places it in a command argument.
remediation.suggestion: Move credential setup outside the agent session and accept secrets through protected interactive input or an operating-system credential store.

remediation.issue: Wallet private keys are stored in a plaintext hidden environment file.
remediation.suggestion: Use hardware-backed signing or an operating-system keychain, restrict file permissions, and document key rotation and revocation procedures.

remediation.issue: Users can bypass a limited token safety check before an irreversible purchase.
remediation.suggestion: Require contract verification and comprehensive token checks for every purchase. Do not allow phrase-based bypasses for unverified contracts.

remediation.issue: A persistent automation flag removes per-transaction terminal confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Require a fresh, transaction-bound approval containing chain, wallet, tokens, amount, slippage, fees, and expiration for every financial action.

remediation.issue: Installation uses an unpinned global npm package.
remediation.suggestion: Pin an audited gmgn-cli version and integrity hash, then verify the installed binary before any credential or trading operation.

remediation.issue: IPv6 troubleshooting enumerates interfaces and contacts a third-party IP service.
remediation.suggestion: Request user consent before diagnostics and prefer local checks that do not disclose the public address to another service.

content.user_title: Execute GMGN Token Swaps and Strategy Orders
content.value_statement: Manual token trading across wallets and chains requires careful parameter handling. This skill prepares GMGN CLI operations with validation, quotes, and confirmation checkpoints.
actual_capabilities: Prepares and submits single token swaps on supported Solana and EVM networks.
Runs concurrent swaps across as many as 100 API-bound wallets.
Retrieves swap quotes, order status, and recommended gas prices.
Creates, lists, and cancels limit, stop-loss, take-profit, and trailing strategy orders.
Validates address formats, amount units, chain restrictions, and selected token security fields.
Formats confirmations and receipts with converted amounts and block-explorer links.
limitations: GMGN CLI and an API key are required; signed operations also require the linked wallet private key.
Blockchain transactions are irreversible and may incur slippage, gas fees, or failed execution costs.
Token names are not resolved, and the built-in safety check covers only honeypot status and rug ratio.
Anti-MEV and strategy features vary by chain, and some networks support only limited order types.

use_cases.title: Confirm a Single Swap
use_cases.description: Prepare a quoted token swap, review resolved addresses and fees, then submit after explicit approval.

use_cases.title: Manage Exit Strategies
use_cases.description: Create and monitor take-profit, stop-loss, or trailing orders for an existing token position.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Wallet Batches
use_cases.description: Prepare consistent trades across several linked wallets while preserving per-wallet amounts and results.

prompt_templates.prompt: Quote swapping [amount] [input token] to [output token] on [chain] from [wallet]. Do not submit a transaction.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Confirmed Swap
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a swap of [amount] [input token] for [output token] on [chain]. Validate addresses, run safety checks, and show confirmation first.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Protected Exit
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a [take-profit or stop-loss] order for [token] on [chain] at [trigger]. Show amount, slippage, fees, and expiry before submission.

prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a multi-wallet swap on [chain] using these wallets and amounts: [details]. Add [conditions], validate every address, and require final confirmation.

output_examples.output: Quote prepared: estimated token output, minimum output, slippage, wallet, and fees. No transaction was submitted.

output_examples.input: Sell 50 percent of a token balance for USDC.
output_examples.output: Confirmation required: verified chain and addresses, percentage amount, estimated USDC proceeds, slippage, and fees.

output_examples.input: Check the result of a submitted swap.
output_examples.output: Swap confirmed: human-readable spent and received amounts, transaction link, and order identifier.

best_practices: Verify contract addresses independently and complete token safety checks before every purchase.
Review chain, wallet, smallest-unit conversion, slippage, fees, and expected output before confirming.
Use small test amounts, anti-MEV protection where supported, and fresh approval for every transaction.
anti_patterns: Do not send API keys or private keys through chat, command arguments, logs, or screenshots.
Do not identify tokens by name alone or skip contract verification because a trade is urgent.
Do not enable unattended trade submission or retry failed transactions without renewed confirmation.

faq.question: Does this skill move real funds?
faq.answer: Yes. Swap and strategy creation commands can authorize irreversible blockchain transactions after confirmation.

faq.question: Which credentials are required?
faq.answer: An API key is required. Swap and most strategy operations also require the private key linked to the wallet.

faq.question: Can it find a token from its name?
faq.answer: No. Provide and independently verify the token contract address before preparing a trade.

faq.question: Which networks are supported?
faq.answer: The documentation covers Solana, BSC, Base, Ethereum, Robinhood, Arc, and Stable, with feature differences between networks.

faq.question: Can it trade across multiple wallets?
faq.answer: Yes. Multi-swap supports up to 100 wallets that are already bound to the GMGN API key.

faq.question: Can a completed swap be reversed?
faq.answer: No. Confirmed blockchain transactions are irreversible, so review every parameter and expected cost before approval.
